pqt8ek: Even If It Works, We Must Ask for Whom: text to interpret
11wbxt: Original SpanishCue material; the situations and data are for teaching, not real news or official exam texts.
rrj14m: The municipality has announced an app that lets people book appointments without standing in line. Although the project is still in its trial phase, its promoters already present it as the end of bureaucracy. The tool offers an obvious improvement: those who have a connection and know how to use it can choose a time slot in a few minutes. It would be absurd to deny that advantage. The problem begins when a solution that is convenient for part of the population becomes the only entry point for everyone.
biwm6h: The office assures that it will keep a help phone line. However, the phone only serves to explain how to complete the digital booking; it does not let you get an appointment directly. Even though there is talk of support, the decision requires having your own device or asking for help. Some people accept that a relative handles the procedure, but that dependence can reveal information they would prefer to keep to themselves. Privacy does not consist only of a database being protected: it also includes being able to carry out procedures without involuntary intermediaries.
ag1e41: Those who defend the app respond that any change requires an adjustment period. They are right, although that argument does not determine how long the transition should last or who bears its cost. No matter how many workshops are organized, there will still be people who cannot or do not want to use the tool. Even if everyone learned, they could lose their connection on the day of the appointment. An accessible administration needs to anticipate those situations without treating them as personal failings of its users.
1wydg2o: The most reasonable proposal is not to withdraw the app, but to evaluate the complete service. It would be necessary to measure how many people manage to complete the procedure, how long it takes them, and what difficulties they encounter in each channel. If only completed digital bookings are counted, those who abandon the process disappear from the statistics. A technology can work correctly and still be part of an unjust system. That is the question the data should help us answer.
